contributions.statement: Expect agent-written JUnit tests on low-maintainability Java classes to kill fewer mutants, so run mutation testing (PIT) on those classes rather than trusting coverage.
contributions.evidence: Table I/II: Java median mutation score 34.8% (CH<6) to 95.1% (CH>=9.8); Spearman rho +.21 for Java mutation, line coverage ns. Single-shot, one model, competitive-programming files, mutation measured only where tests passed; vendor co-authors and proprietary metric.
relative_to: code complexity lowers LLM test-generation effectiveness (known pre-2026)

contributions.statement: Low-maintainability Java files cost about 45% more input tokens than healthy ones, beyond what their size explains.
contributions.evidence: Table III: rho -.28 to -.30 Java across four tokenizers, partial for SLOC -.24 to -.34; Table I bin medians.

reason: High-COI correlational study on toy files with weak effect sizes; the token-cost correlation is real but not actionable beyond 'refactor messy code', so treat the mutation-score link as a hypothesis.
